topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the scope of the lecture on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate immune recognition through PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of how the innate immune system detects foreign microbes and host tissue damage using germline-encoded pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: PRR families, downstream signaling, and the inflammasome
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific classes of pattern recognition receptors, their intracellular signaling mechanisms, and the assembly of the inflammasome complex.

topics.label: Inflammatory mobilization, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic complications
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells direct immune cell trafficking into tissues and lymph nodes, as well as the pathological consequences of uncontrolled systemic inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the passive and active mechanisms that terminate inflammation, drive tissue healing, and maintain chronic protective structures like granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and states the topic of the following lecture.
